title: Gowers products of a $\pm1$-valued function take values $\pm1$
statement:
Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ be a Boolean-valued function, and let $F : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$, $F(x) = (-1)^{f(x)}$, be its $\pm1$ lift. Then for every order $k \ge 0$, every base point $x \in \{0,1\}^n$, and all direction vectors $h_1, \ldots, h_k \in \{0,1\}^n$, the order-$k$ Gowers product satisfies
\[
  \mathrm{GP}(F, k, x, h_1, \ldots, h_k) \in \{1, -1\}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: F is the ±1 lift of f, F(x) = (-1)^{f(x)}
replaced:
If $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ and $F = (-1)^f$ is its $\pm 1$ lift, then for
every $k$, $x$, and $h_1,\ldots,h_k$,
$\mathrm{GP}(F, k, x, h_1,\ldots,h_k) \in \{1, -1\}$.
